clue.text: Stage qualification

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a step or level in a scale or process
second meaning: an award from a university

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the words suggest a theatrical or acting qualification; they are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a step in a progression (to some extent) and an academic award conferred by a university.

clue.text: Fed up? Beam getting pay

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: Someone fed up with their wages, perhaps a builder working with beams.
explanation.definitionFit: To defray costs is to pay or settle them, a formal synonym for meeting an expense.

clue.text: Farm worker playing Grieg solo

indicators.note: playing a piece lets the performer interpret it freely, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A farmhand entertains themselves performing a solo piece by the Norwegian composer Grieg.
explanation.definitionFit: A goose-girl is a girl who tends geese on a farm, a traditional farm labourer of folk tales.

clue.text: Sad, as developing Ice Age consumes loch

indicators.note: to consume is to take inside, so one piece is placed within the other
something developing changes its form, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
L is the map abbreviation for loch or lake

explanation.surface: A melancholy picture of an ice age engulfing a Scottish lake as it advances.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged ICE AGE becomes E_EGIAC with L slipped in after the first E. A loch is a Scottish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegiac describes the mournful tone of an elegy, so it means sad or lamenting.

clue.text: Cryptically, what indicates pots could be a barrier?

parts.note: surface reading: some sign or label pointing out cooking pots
setter's reading: in crossword language, 'pots' is a word you get by turning a four-letter word for halt the other way, so the instruction for it names the answer

explanation.surface: A puzzling question about what signals pots and whether it could serve as a barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: In a crossword, a reversal indicator such as 'back' placed beside 'stop' would clue POTS; the answer is that very instruction, BACK STOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A backstop is a fence or screen behind a playing area, and more broadly a safeguard or barrier of last resort.

clue.text: Having nothing to do — certainly not tied up!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: idle, with time on one's hands
second meaning: literally, a rope end that is unfastened

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tied up' means busy, so not tied up is idle again; the exclamation flags the literal picture of a dangling rope.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means idle or unoccupied, and taken literally describes a cord whose tip is unfastened.

clue.text: Fish or CIA pork supply

indicators.note: read as 'supplely', bending flexibly, so these letters are bent into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A menu choice between fish and a pork supply provided by the American intelligence agency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like a noun meaning provision; it is the adverb of supple, meaning flexibly.
explanation.definitionFit: Koi carp are ornamental coloured carp bred in Japan and kept in garden ponds, an example of fish.

clue.text: Former PM in bind

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Liz ..., briefly UK Prime Minister in 2022
second meaning: to tie up tightly, as a cook does a chicken

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an ex-premier in trouble; 'bind' is a separate verb meaning tie.
explanation.definitionFit: Liz Truss held office as British Prime Minister for seven weeks, and to truss is to tie securely.

clue.text: Excuses vacuous politicians keeping on message

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside, so the other pieces sit within
vacuous means empty, so the word loses its interior and only its two ends remain

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
re means on or concerning
a text is a phone message

explanation.surface: A cynical jab at empty-headed politicians who stick to their talking points to dodge blame.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretexts are false reasons offered to hide the real motive, so they are excuses.

clue.text: Fruity dessert journalist took in

parts.note: a fool is a pudding of puréed fruit and cream
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A reporter wolfing down a fruit pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Took in' reads as eating; it means deceived.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone in is to deceive or trick them, which is what fooled means.

clue.text: Fellow I help to get better cosmetic treatment

parts.note: a fellow is a man
taken as written
to cure is to make well

explanation.surface: A man says he helps others look better through a beauty treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: A manicure is a beauty treatment for the hands and nails, a kind of cosmetic care.

clue.text: Yank with ordinary coffee

parts.note: a Yank is an American
O is an abbreviation for ordinary

explanation.surface: An American ordering a plain cup of coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' could be a verb meaning pull; here it is a noun for an American.
explanation.definitionFit: An Americano is espresso diluted with hot water, a common café drink.

clue.text: The military, having weapons, uses coercion

parts.note: armed means carrying weapons
forces means compels by pressure

explanation.surface: A description of the army as heavily equipped and given to coercion.
explanation.definitionFit: The armed forces are a nation's army, navy and air force taken together, its military services.

clue.text: "I will" said in part of church

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the words are judged by how they are pronounced

parts.note: the contraction of these words is pronounced like a church passage

explanation.surface: A bride or groom saying 'I will' during a church wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: The wedding picture is apt: vows are made at the end of the walk up the church.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is the passage between the pews in a church, a part of the building.

clue.text: Muppet coins? Or, surprisingly, a genuine pay-out

indicators.note: something that turns out surprisingly is not in the expected form, so these letters land in an unexpected order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Does a puppet character have toy money, or is this, surprisingly, a real payment?
explanation.walkthrough: Income Support is a British state benefit for people on low incomes.
explanation.definitionFit: Income Support is a UK government benefit paid to people on low incomes, a real welfare payment.

clue.text: Unhappy lovers use us

indicators.note: unhappy suggests something disturbed and out of sorts, so these letters are disordered

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A complaint that miserable couples exploit people like us.
explanation.definitionFit: Ourselves is the reflexive form of we, standing for us when the speakers are also the object.

clue.text: Lab isn't rebuilt around university in city

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the other letters enclose the single piece
rebuilding puts the parts back together differently, so these letters are reassembled

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A city campus where a laboratory has not yet been reconstructed around the university.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters ISTANB_L take the U just before the final L.
explanation.definitionFit: Istanbul is Turkey's largest city, straddling the Bosporus between Europe and Asia.

clue.text: Unfortunately, pen pals parted? They're often together in the dining room

definitions.text: They're often together in the dining room

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so these letters have fallen out of order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Sad news that two pen friends have split up, though some pairs stay united at the dinner table.
explanation.definitionFit: Salt and pepper are the two condiments usually set side by side on a dining table.

clue.text: Maria upset with one line in overseas correspondence

indicators.note: upset means knocked into disorder, so the letters of the name are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Maria is distressed by a single line in a letter from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmail is post sent by aircraft, the usual way letters travel to other countries.

clue.text: Frontiersman with messy eating habits, might you say?

indicators.note: this asks what you would utter, so the result is judged by pronunciation

parts.note: a pastry smeared on the side of one's head is the mark of a messy eater

explanation.surface: A rough frontier settler who eats sloppily.
explanation.walkthrough: A comic picture of a messy eater: food on the side of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer was one of the first settlers to open up new territory, a frontiersman.

clue.text: Afterthought, getting charitable donations for religious works

parts.note: PS, postscript, is an afterthought added to a letter
alms are gifts to the poor

explanation.surface: A last-minute appeal for charity to support a church's work.
explanation.definitionFit: The Psalms are the sacred songs of the Old Testament, religious works of poetry.

clue.text: Tree produced deal and resin, intially

indicators.note: something produced is made into a new form, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a misspelling of initially, meaning only the opening letter of the word is taken

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A tree yielding timber and sap.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal is a softwood timber, which strengthens the tree picture; here it is only letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The alder is a deciduous tree of the birch family that grows near water.

clue.text: Some ships in shipyard? How spiffing!

indicators.note: in means contained within, so the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: An admiring cry at the sight of vessels in a dockyard.
explanation.definitionFit: Dhows are traditional sailing vessels of the Arabian Sea and Indian Ocean, a type of ship.

clue.text: Dinosaurs, perhaps, in ancient mist? Yes, in a way

indicators.note: in a way suggests something done after a fashion, loosely, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: ancient means old
fog is a thick mist
the three letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Musing whether prehistoric creatures are lurking in an age-old haze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dinosaurs' are not the prehistoric beasts but people with outdated views, which 'perhaps' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinosaurs is slang for people stuck in the past, which is what old fogeys are.

clue.text: Italian in past times exhibiting close male friendship

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: BCE, before the common era, marks dates long ago
a Roman is an Italian from Rome

explanation.surface: A man from Italy in olden days showing a deep friendship with another man.
explanation.definitionFit: A bromance is a close, affectionate but non-sexual friendship between two men.

clue.text: Opposing positions taken with foul insect

parts.note: west and east are opposite compass points
foul in the sense of wicked

explanation.surface: Two sides of an argument both disgusted by a nasty bug.
explanation.walkthrough: W and E are compass points directly opposite each other, as on a bridge table.
explanation.definitionFit: A weevil is a small beetle with a long snout, a pest of grain and stored food.

clue.text: Having no enthusiasm, needing to remember what shopping to get?

definitions.text: needing to remember what shopping to get?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, playful: without a written shopping record, so it must all be memorised

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical second reading, splitting the word into a noun plus the suffix meaning without.
explanation.definitionFit: Listless means lethargic and lacking energy, and jokingly describes a shopper who has no written note of items.

clue.text: Catastrophe of monarch who was executed by sibling

parts.note: Charles I, Carolus Rex the First, was beheaded in 1649
sis is short for sister

explanation.surface: A grim royal tale of a king put to death by his own brother or sister.
explanation.walkthrough: CR (Carolus Rex) is the Latin royal cipher of King Charles, and Charles I was the English king executed in 1649.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisis is a time of acute danger or disaster, a close synonym for catastrophe.
